angle: The commander plays before he's cast: Edgar's eminence engine runs from the command zone for zero mana from turn 1, so every real decision in this deck is about the one turn he stops being free — the median-turn-6 alpha-strike pivot, or the tutor-hidden Vito knockout you present only in a dead window.

departments.headline: CAST EVERYTHING BUT HIM
departments.dek: What is the strongest card in a deck that begins every game with it face up and never pays a mana for it? Edgar Markov makes a Vampire for every Vampire you cast — from the command zone, from turn 1, for free — and the whole game is deciding which turn he finally sends the bill.

callouts.title: BANK BODIES
callouts.text: Turns 1–3: deploy down the 8/19/19 curve of one-, two-, and three-drop Vampires. Every cast is two bodies — the creature and the eminence token — and the payoffs find themselves: a lord or Vampire payoff is drawn by turn 6 in 67.7% of simulated games. Do not cast Edgar. The engine costs nothing while he sits at home.

callouts.title: LAYER THE DRAINS
callouts.text: Turns 4–6: add the pieces that make width lethal against three life totals — Sanctum Seeker and Bloodletter of Aclazotz (a drain engine is drawn by turn 6 in 62.5% of games), a token doubler (42.4%), Grave Pact riding token deaths. Deploy in waves under wrath-math: commit what wins before the near-certain sweeper, and let eminence be the rebuild — one token per cast, no recast tax, forever.

callouts.title: TAKE THE WINDOW
callouts.text: Turn 6 and later: pick your pivot. Cast Edgar (median cast turn 6) into a protected alpha strike — his attack trigger puts a +1/+1 counter on every Vampire you control, and resolving him turns Flawless Maneuver and Deflecting Swat free — or tutor the Vito half onto a gain-on-loss piece already in play and end the game on the stack instead.

captions.Edgar Markov: **THE ENGINE:** eminence makes a 1/1 Vampire per other Vampire spell you cast — while he is in the command zone. The deck's core engine is online before your first land drop and no removal spell in the format can touch it.
captions.Knight of the Ebon Legion: **TURN ONE, TWO BODIES:** the tribe's best one-drop, and its end-step counter clause — someone lost 4 or more life — is a bar this deck's drains clear constantly.
captions.Sanctum Seeker: **WHY WIDTH WORKS:** each attacking Vampire drains every opponent for 1. Incremental combat damage doesn't scale to three defenses; each-opponent triggers do.

pilot_tips.text: Never cast Edgar just because you hit six mana — cast him the turn you intend to swing wide with protection held, because his engine runs at full power from the zone and his body is the pivot, not the plan.

departments.pull_quote: The engine costs zero. The commander is the pivot, not the plan.

departments.headline: THE ZONE IS THE ENGINE
departments.dek: The command zone usually means guaranteed access to a card you still have to pay for. What is it worth when the ability works from the zone itself — and casting your commander is the optional part?
departments.body: Four teaching blocks and one coaching block. ONE — the guarantee, inverted (✓): eminence states its zones and functions from them (CR 113.6b: 'An ability that states which zones it functions in functions only from those zones.'), so this deck's engine is not merely guaranteed access — it is guaranteed operation. No mulligan finds it because no hand needs it; no removal answers it because no permanent carries it. TWO — the tax ladder (✓ CR 903.8): {3}{R}{W}{B} on the first cast, 8 on the second, 10 on the third — set beside the goldfish's mean available mana of 5.362 on turn 6 to show what each rung really costs this manabase. The wrinkle unique to this deck: recasting is genuinely optional, because a dead Edgar keeps making tokens from the zone — the tax buys back the alpha-strike trigger and the free-protection condition, nothing else. THREE — colour identity, with a scar to show (✓ CR 903.4): Mardu governs all 100 cards including lands' rules text, and this deck was caught by it at the border — the pilot's physical list arrived with Crosis's Catacombs, whose blue identity is illegal under Edgar; ingestion bounced it and Nomad Outpost took the slot at the pilot's direction (HISTORY.md). Print the catch proudly: the rule most players wave at is one this very issue enforced. FOUR — the clock (✓ CR 903.10a): 21 commander damage is a coincidence here, not a plan — a 4/4 first-striker needs five connects even before counters, and the deck's real clocks are seven-wide drains and a 38-trigger loop. The coaching block (★) is protect-vs-race with the eminence twist: normal commander-insurance math asks what protecting the commander is worth; here the free protection suite (Flawless Maneuver, Deflecting Swat at {0}) only switches on when Edgar resolves — so the insurance and the pivot arrive on the same turn, and before it, Boros Charm and hard-cast Maneuver cost the exact mana the curve wants for Vampires. Budget accordingly.

captions.Edgar Markov: **THE COMMANDER FILE:** {3}{R}{W}{B}, Mardu identity, goldfish mean cast 6.613 (median 6, 52.1% by turn 6) — and an eminence ability that has been working since before turn 1.
captions.Flawless Maneuver: **PRICED IN EDGAR:** free only while you control a commander. The eminence plan keeps him zoned until turn 6, so this reads {2}{W} for the first five turns — the deck's central protection tension.
captions.Nomad Outpost: **THE LEGAL REPLACEMENT:** it holds the slot Crosis's Catacombs illegally occupied — a blue-identity land under a Mardu commander, caught at ingestion. Colour identity governs the 99, lands included.

pilot_tips.text: Count Deflecting Swat as part of Edgar's casting cost math — the turn he resolves, it flips from a three-mana trick to free interaction, which is a real argument for an earlier Edgar against a known combo seat.

departments.pull_quote: Removal cannot touch the command zone. The table's only answer to eminence is to end the game.

departments.headline: THE BODY COUNT
departments.dek: Ten thousand seeded runs, no opponents, no mercy: what does a zero-mana engine actually produce, and why does a six-drop commander have a median cast of turn 6 on 34 lands? The chart answers both — and names the tempo tax the manabase pays.

callouts.title: BODIES WITHOUT A COMMANDER
callouts.text: Mean bodies: 1.884 by turn 3, 4.177 by turn 6, 6.359 by turn 10 — with zero mana ever spent on Edgar. That is the eminence dividend, and the model doesn't even count doubler multiplication beyond parsed token text.

callouts.title: MEDIAN CAST: TURN 6
callouts.text: Edgar lands by turn 6 in 52.1% of games (mean 6.613); the histogram's spike is turn 6 at 3,811 of 10,000 runs, and 16.0% of games never cast him by turn 10 — and lose nothing but the alpha strike for it.

callouts.title: THE 2.8% INFINITE
callouts.text: Vito plus a gain-on-loss half assembles naturally in 2.8% of games by turn 6 and 4.9% by turn 10. Print it big: the infinite is insurance, not plan A — and the three tutors that change that math are not modeled here at all.

callouts.title: THE TAPPED-LAND TAX
callouts.text: 16 of 34 lands can enter tapped; land drops fall to 59.2% by turn 6 and mean available mana is 5.362 — which is the whole story of why a six-mana commander waits. The curve lives at one, two, and three on purpose.

captions.Bontu's Monument: **LAB NOTE:** cost reducers, rituals, and tutors are not modeled — every figure on this page is the floor. The real deck casts more, drains more, and assembles the knockout more often than the chart admits.

pilot_tips.text: Lead Ancient Tomb into a two-drop Vampire whenever the opener offers it — two colourless on turn 1 is a body plus a banked eminence token before anyone else has moved.

departments.pull_quote: Half the games cast Edgar by turn 6. Every game runs his engine from turn 1.
departments.note: The stated-assumptions box is non-negotiable and earns its keep twice here: the model simulates resource development, not games (no interaction, no removal), and it does not model the tutor suite — so the 2.8%/4.9% infinite figure is natural assembly only, exactly as the strategic frame frames it. Cite every number exactly as goldfish_metrics.json reports it: 0.521, 6.613, 1.884, 4.177, 6.359, 0.592, 5.362, 0.028, 0.049. Seed 42, 10,000 iterations.

departments.headline: FOUR WAYS TO BLEED A TABLE
departments.dek: Two engines you'll run every game and two knockouts you'll tutor for once — all four checker-passed against the June 19, 2026 rules. The famous loop is real, the token math is exact, the declare-step drain kills before blockers exist, and the second infinite comes with its weakness printed on the stamp.

callouts.title: FIVE BODIES, TWO MANA
callouts.text: Stack 002, the everyday engine: Gifted Aetherborn for {B}{B} with Edgar zoned and both doublers out. Eminence triggers once, Anointed Procession and Mondrak double it in either order — 1 becomes 2 becomes 4, the checker confirmed order doesn't matter — and all four tokens enter with Socialite counters. Five new bodies, one cast. Just as verified: tokens are created, not cast, so eminence never re-triggers on them. FULL DOSSIER: JUDGE'S DESK A-002 →

callouts.title: FOURTEEN AT DECLARE
callouts.text: Stack 003, the fair kill: seven Vampires attack with Sanctum Seeker and Bloodletter of Aclazotz among them. Seven Seeker triggers, each opponent's loss doubled on your turn: 14 from every opponent at declare attackers, before a single blocker is named — and the checker confirmed the opponent at 14 hits exactly 0 and is gone by state-based actions mid-combat. Your gain is 7, never doubled: Bloodletter reads opponents only. FULL DOSSIER: JUDGE'S DESK A-003 →

callouts.title: THE 38-TRIGGER TABLE-KILL
callouts.text: Stack 001, the marquee: Exquisite Blood plus Vito, seeded by a 2-point lifelink hit. Each Vito trigger is a new object targeted fresh, so you walk the drain across the table in any order — 6, 13, and 19 resolutions clear opponents at 12, 25, and 38 life, 38 iterations total, and a mid-loop death never breaks the chain because the killing loss still triggers your enchantment. You end at 105 life having spent nothing. FULL DOSSIER: JUDGE'S DESK A-001 →

callouts.title: THE FRAGILE TWIN
callouts.text: Stack 004, verified on its own terms: Bloodthirsty Conqueror's trigger matches Exquisite Blood's word for word — the checker confirmed '(Damage causes loss of life.)' is reminder text, not a requirement — and 13 iterations from a 3-life seed killed a 9- and a 30-life opponent with zero overkill. The honest cost, printed at full size: the gain half is a 5/5 creature, so every iteration's priority window admits instant-speed removal. Strictly more fragile than the enchantment version, and now you know exactly why. FULL DOSSIER: JUDGE'S DESK A-004 →

captions.Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose: **THE HINGE:** both verified infinites route through this three-mana body — every life gain becomes targeted loss. He is the deck's most removal-magnetic card, and the cheap, recastable half of either loop.
captions.Exquisite Blood: **THE RESILIENT HALF:** an enchantment, immune to the creature removal and wraths a bracket-4 table actually holds — stack 001's loop needed Vito to survive exactly one priority window.
captions.Bloodthirsty Conqueror: **THE FRAGILE HALF:** same loop, on a body — stack 004's verified finding is a removal window every single iteration. The flying deathtouch 5/5 is for the fair game this card also dominates.
captions.Mondrak, Glory Dominus: **THE MULTIPLIER:** half of stack 002's 1-becomes-4 arithmetic, on a 4/4 that can sacrifice two spare tokens to buy indestructible — a doubler that survives the sweeper it invites.

pilot_tips.text: Never wait for a big lifegain event to start the loop — stack 001's full-table kill was seeded by this card's ordinary 2-point lifelink connect.

departments.pull_quote: Thirty-eight triggers, zero mana spent, three dead opponents — and the killing blow still fed the chain.
departments.note: The issue's peak and its most ambitious layout: run A-001 as the centerpiece scene with the three per-opponent resolution counts (6, 13, 19) as the numbered spine, A-002 and A-003 as the everyday-engine spreads before it, A-004 as the honest-cost coda. The map-key carries ♥ life and a token glyph. Only these four checker-passed stacks may be stated as fact; the Sanguine Bond mirrors are Upgrade Watch's problem and are flagged there as unverified.

departments.headline: NO QUIET GAMES
departments.dek: Eminence banks a visible body every time you cast a spell — so 'I haven't done anything' is unsellable from turn 1. When your threat level is structural, what exactly is a deflection budget for, and what do you buy with the last of it?

callouts.title: THREAT WINDOW
callouts.text: The board state that flips you to archenemy: Vito visible next to open black mana, or Sanctum Seeker plus five-or-more attackers once anyone does the stack-003 math out loud. Edgar himself announces the alpha strike the moment he's cast — which is why you cast him the turn it kills a player, not a turn earlier. Take the label when it pays.

callouts.title: THE KILL ORDER
callouts.text: What the table answers first, in order: Vito dies on sight — both contained infinites route through him and a bracket-4 pod knows it. Then the drain engines, then Grave Pact and the doublers. The lords mostly survive, and they're the wrong things to protect anyway: protect the pieces that scale, not the ones that pump.

callouts.title: THE CONCEALMENT DOCTRINE
callouts.text: Your tutors are combo protection: Demonic and Vampiric put the missing half where no removal spell reaches — your hand and your library. Never present both halves in the same open-mana window. Land the half the table undervalues first (Exquisite Blood alone reads as a lifegain trinket), and complete the pair the turn the answer-holder taps out or spends the wrath.

captions.Demonic Tutor: **THE ARMOR:** the table knows what a tutor with Vito on board means — but an assumption is not a target, and a card in hand cannot be Dispatched.
captions.Grave Pact: **THE RESENTMENT ENGINE:** every token death forces each opponent to sacrifice — value that makes enemies. Fire it while your deflection budget still has a balance.

pilot_tips.text: Cast Exquisite Blood while it still reads as a lifegain trinket — alone it draws no removal, and once it's in play only the cheap, recastable half of the loop is ever exposed again.

departments.pull_quote: Telegraphed is not the same as answerable.

departments.headline: PIVOT OR PATIENCE
departments.dek: One turn asks whether six mana is Edgar or two more Vampires; the other asks what a tutor is really for when everyone at the table knows what you'd fetch. Read each board, commit out loud, and only then read the bench's ruling.

callouts.title: HOW TO PLAY ALONG
callouts.text: Cover the recommendation box. Read the board, pick a branch, say it out loud — the signals and coalition risks are printed with each branch so you can argue with them. Being wrong on this page is free; being wrong at the table costs a game.

callouts.title: TURN 6: THE ALPHA WINDOW
callouts.text: Decision 001. Six mana after the Knight resolves, four banked tokens, a draw-go player with four untapped lands, an aggro seat at 12 and tapped out. Edgar now, a bigger board, or a smaller board with protection held? Every branch is defensible. One is right.

callouts.title: TURN 8: THE HIDDEN HALF
callouts.text: Decision 002. Vito survived a full rotation, Demonic Tutor in hand, eight lands untapped — and the control seat has held five mana all game. Fetch and present, fetch and hide, or hold the tutor as an answer? The verified kill is real; the question is whether this is its window.

captions.Swiftfoot Boots: **THE QUIET ENABLER:** hexproof plus haste for one to equip is the difference between an Edgar who pivots the game and an Edgar who eats the removal the table saved six turns for.

pilot_tips.text: Ask which wrath you actually fear before leaning on Flawless Maneuver — indestructible beats destroy effects, and does nothing against Toxic Deluge's -X/-X or an exile sweeper.

departments.pull_quote: An assumption is not a target.
departments.note: Render both decision artifacts in full — board, question, all branches with signals and coalition risk, recommendation revealed only after the branches, per the artifact contract. Neither headline nor callout may telegraph a recommendation; 'PIVOT OR PATIENCE' names the tension, not the answer. Decision 002 is the concealment doctrine's teaching home — the politics spread points here.

departments.headline: WHO DRAINS THE DRAINER
departments.dek: The sweeper is near-certain over four players, the taxes halve your two-spell turns, and a single 'players can't gain life' effect switches off both infinites. But which half of your deck survives each of these — and can you name your outs before you sit down?

threats.read: Assume the wrath and deploy in waves: commit exactly what wins, no further. Your rebuild is structural — every post-wrath Vampire cast re-banks an eminence token with no recast tax, and Bloodghast returns on a land drop. Hold one protection spell for the committed turn, and remember your own Olivia's Wrath is a second alpha strike against their creature suite. The unrebuildable loss is Edgar himself: the next cast is 8.

Know exactly which half of your deck dies: 'players can't gain life' turns off both verified infinites and blanks the lifelink bodies — but the combat drain plan is life LOSS. Sanctum Seeker's trigger and Bloodletter's doubling function untouched, so stack 003's 14-per-opponent arithmetic survives intact. Stop tutoring for Exquisite Blood; start tutoring for the hate's answer.

You are the forced beatdown: the 19-and-19 two/three-drop core is exactly the many-cheap-spells profile that Sphere effects halve, and your mana is already taxed — 16 of 34 lands enter tapped and mean available mana is 5.362 on turn 6. Race the lock's assembly, identify the one piece that beats YOU (usually the cast tax, since eminence pays per cast), and aim your removal there. Edgar stays zoned longer here.

Your combat clock does not beat a tuned combo turn — mean bodies 6.359 by turn 10 — so answer economy inverts: the last profitable moment for held interaction is now. The white removal and Deflecting Swat matter most, with the standing tension that Swat is free only once Edgar resolves — a real argument for an earlier, unprotected Edgar against a known combo seat. Your counter-clock is the tutored Vito line.

pilot_tips.text: Feed Bloodghast to Diabolic Intent and Grave Pact without hesitation — it can't block anyway, and it returns on any land drop, fetch cracks included.
Cast Olivia's Wrath as an attack, not a rescue — with a wide Vampire board its -X/-X clears every blocker and misses your entire army.

departments.pull_quote: The hate card turns off the loops — and leaves the declare-step drain untouched. Life loss isn't lifegain.

departments.headline: EVERY CAST COUNTS TWICE
departments.dek: Sixty-three spells whose common cost is hidden: each Vampire cast also prints a body from the command zone. Twenty-nine threats, three tutors, thirteen answers, a manabase hauling 49 black pips — ranked by load, led by the six cards the whole issue orbits, with the twelve slots the role taxonomy famously cannot see.

cards: Vito, Thorn of the Dusk Rose

roster.role: The drains that scale to three opponents
The token engine and its amplifiers
Lords, anthems, and the alpha-strike kit

cards: Midgar, City of Mako // Reactor Raid

captions.Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth: **THE PATCH:** every land becomes a Swamp under a manabase owing 49 black pips across 35 black spells — your painlands and white sources all pay the tribe's real bill.
captions.Welcoming Vampire: **THE STEADY REFILL:** a card per turn whenever another power-2-or-less creature enters — every eminence token switches it on.

pilot_tips.text: Pay Rite of Oblivion's sacrifice with an eminence token — a nearly-free exile that flashes back for a second one later.

departments.pull_quote: Twenty-nine threats, one sweeper of your own, and an engine no wrath can reach.
departments.note: Rank matters: the kill package leads because it is why the bracket floor reads 4; mana closes. Full card blurbs render from manual_prose.card_roles — the remaining 25 lands beyond the marked-cards group render there. The 36-card physical sideboard renders as its own labeled strip (this deck's accessories are a bench, not tokens), pointing to Upgrade Watch for the rulings. Print the honesty note: 12 cards — including Exquisite Blood, Grave Pact, and Anointed Procession — have no role-taxonomy entry; absence of a role chip is a limit of the taxonomy, not of the card, and we say so in print.

departments.headline: NINETY-THREE HANDS
departments.dek: Who gets the credit page when ninety-three artists split 131 cards and the leader holds four? Nobody — and that's the story. This collection was assembled card by card across a decade of printings, so the feature follows the deck's own plot: the hand that painted the swing turn.

featured.note: Two entries, two copies, no inflation — and they happen to be both halves of this deck's signature turn: Bloodletter of Aclazotz, the doubler that turns stack 003's seven triggers into 14 from each opponent, and Akroma's Will, the spell that makes the same alpha strike unanswerable. One artist, by pure collection accident, painted the declare step and its protection. In a 93-artist book that coincidence is the closest thing to a byline the swing turn will ever get.

also_worth_noting.note: The co-leader at four entries — Akroma's Memorial, Arcane Signet, Diabolic Intent, and the benched Leering Onlooker. Three of four in the 99, spanning a seven-drop haymaker to a two-mana rock.
Four entries and a specialty: three of them are lands (Castle Locthwain, Luxury Suite, Savai Triome), plus the benched Throne of the God-Pharaoh. The manabase's house painter.
Three entries, all maindeck, all nocturnes — Blood Crypt, Silent Clearing, Twilight Prophet. The deck's mood board in three frames.

Three entries — two of which are Strefan, Maurer Progenitor twice, in different printings: the maindeck copy and the spare in the box. Painting the same Vampire for two different shelves is its own kind of credit.

captions.Bloodletter of Aclazotz: **THE DOUBLER, SIGNED:** Manzanedo's bat god presides over stack 003 — on your turn, every opponent's loss doubles, and 7 becomes 14 before blockers exist.
captions.Akroma's Will: **THE SHIELD, SAME HAND:** Manzanedo also painted the swing turn's protection — with Edgar on the battlefield you take both modes, and every lifelink point it grants is a Vito trigger.

departments.pull_quote: We count the cards, not the copies — four Swamps are one credit.
departments.note: The analysis reports no standout (lead artist: 4 entries — its own note says tell a breadth story) and an empty drop-run list, so no bought-whole caveat applies: this concentration pattern is honest breadth, not structure. Respect the per-entry notes verbatim: Swamp is 1 entry/4 copies (per-copy would inflate Dimitar Marinski), Unholy Officiant and Vampire Nocturnus are 1 entry/2 copies each. Totals for the Art File box: 93 artists, 131 entries, 136 copies, 1 borderless, 0 foils, 20 legendary frames, 9 showcases. The featured pick is editorial — chosen for the story, counts recomputed by the renderer.

departments.headline: NEVER KEEP FOR EDGAR
departments.dek: 81.4% of first sevens are keeps at 0.224 mulligans per game — and your commander is none of the reason. He's face up in the zone before your first decision, so the drill is pure engine-hand arithmetic: enablers over payoffs, untapped over tapped, and four rulings to argue with.

hands.why: Three lands that can all enter untapped, two cheap Vampires (each worth two bodies), a lord, and a refill. This is the enabler-heavy shape that wins the engine-hand test — the payoffs find themselves: a lord or payoff is drawn by turn 6 in 67.7% of games.

Two lands reads risky until you price the mana: Tomb plus Ring is four mana on turn 1. The deck-facts nuance that saves this keep — 16 of 34 lands can enter tapped, so a two-land hand needs its lands untapped. These are.

Three lands, zero plays before turn 4 — in a deck built to bank a token per turn from turn 1 or 2, this hand skips the entire eminence dividend. Payoff-heavy hands ship; the engine is the thing you must actually hold.

hands.verdict: SHIP — the flood the sim would keep
hands.why: The goldfish's mechanical rule keeps 2–5 lands, so this five-lander passes the machine — and the coach overrules it. One spell to cast before turn 4, and protection plus a tutor are luxuries in an opener, not a plan. The badge difference printed honestly: ◆ says keepable, ★ says ship.

captions.Concealed Courtyard: **THE FIRST-THREE-TURNS LAND:** untapped exactly through the land drops when an 8-one-drop, 19-two-drop curve needs it most.

pilot_tips.text: Keep hands where Vampire Interloper is a proud turn-2 play — a 2/1 flier that can't block is pure eminence fuel, and this deck grades openers on casts, not card quality.

departments.pull_quote: He lives in the command zone. Mulligan like he doesn't exist.

departments.headline: THE BENCH REPORT
departments.dek: This deck's future isn't in a preview gallery — it's a 36-card bench the pilot already owns. The analysis rules: one unconditional promotion, two swaps with named trigger conditions, one card that can never legally play, and thirty that stay in the box with reasons attached.

callouts.title: PROMOTE: VISCERA SEER
callouts.text: In for Vampire Interloper, unconditionally, at the next revision. The maindeck role histogram shows zero sac outlets next to Grave Pact and Voldaren Pariah; Seer is a free, instant-speed outlet on a one-mana Vampire body, and the eminence-token trade with Interloper is a wash. Bracket floor: 4 before, 4 after.

callouts.title: CONDITIONAL: SANGUINE BOND
callouts.text: In for Stensia Masquerade — once your pod starts holding creature removal for Vito. Bond's trigger is word-for-word Vito's first ability on an enchantment Swords can't reach, and it pairs with Exquisite Blood or Bloodthirsty Conqueror in the same loop shape stacks 001 and 004 verified for Vito. Say the quiet part at full volume: neither Bond pairing has its own checker-passed stack. Strongly indicated is not verified.

callouts.title: META CALL: KALITAS
callouts.text: Kalitas, Traitor of Ghet in for Vampire Nighthawk when your pod leans on graveyards or death triggers — with Grave Pact forcing sacrifices, Kalitas exiles what dies and pays you a Zombie each time. Nighthawk is the honest cut: duplicated function next to Nighthawk Scavenger.

callouts.title: NEVER: RUNO STROMKIRK
callouts.text: The bench's one unplayable card: {1}{U}{B} — blue identity, illegal under a Mardu commander, the same rule that bounced Crosis's Catacombs at ingestion. It lives in the box as a collection card, and printing that plainly is the point. Also not options: the spare Vito, Strefan, Nocturnus, and Officiant copies — backups, not upgrades.

captions.Viscera Seer: **THE MISSING OUTLET:** the only card in the collection that kills your own creatures on demand — with Grave Pact, each free token becomes an each-opponent edict at instant speed.
captions.Sanguine Bond: **THE UNSTAMPED MIRROR:** Vito's trigger, verbatim, on a five-mana enchantment. The loops it would form mirror the verified ones — and carry no stamp until a stack scenario runs.

pilot_tips.text: When Viscera Seer comes in, re-read Voldaren Pariah — the flip's sacrifice-three cost stops being a fantasy the moment you can convert spare tokens at instant speed.

departments.pull_quote: The famous Bond loops mirror stacks 001 and 004 exactly — and carry no stamp. Strongly indicated is not verified.
departments.note: Source is sideboard_analysis.json, a committed artifact — this issue's Upgrade Watch reads the pilot's own bench rather than the obsolescence index, and says so. All three swaps hold the bracket floor at 4. The aristocrats sub-package (Cruel Celebrant, Indulgent Aristocrat, Master of Dark Rites) gets one paragraph as 'the identity shift in the box' — a direction, not a recommendation, since no pilot_feedback.md states appetite and the strategy corpus has no aristocrats section to cite.

departments.headline: FOUR FILES, FOUR STAMPS
